name: From the yoga of understanding to brahmanirvāṇa (BhG 2.39–72)

stages.name: buddhiyoga in action
stages.gloss: acting established in yoga, attachment abandoned, the same in success and failure
stages.description: The understanding 'according to yoga' (2.39): entitlement to action and not its fruit; equanimity is yoga, yoga is skill in actions; the fruit abandoned, one is freed from the bondage of birth (2.47–51).

stages.name: crossing the thicket of delusion
stages.description: When the understanding crosses the thicket of delusion, one becomes indifferent to what is to be heard and what has been heard (2.52).

stages.name: attaining yoga
stages.description: When the understanding, perplexed by what it has heard, stands unwavering and immovable in samādhi, one attains yoga (2.53).

stages.name: sthitaprajña
stages.description: All desires given up, content in the self by the self; senses withdrawn; unshaken in pain and pleasure; free of 'mine' and 'I'; serenity and peace (2.55–71).

stages.name: brāhmī sthiti and brahmanirvāṇa
stages.gloss: the state of brahman; its nirvāṇa at death
stages.description: Having attained the brāhmī sthiti one is no longer deluded; abiding in it even at death one attains brahmanirvāṇa (2.72).

notes: The order of stages 1–3 follows the text's own 'when … then' clauses (2.52–53); stage 4 answers Arjuna's question at 2.54, and stage 5 is named at 2.72. The Gītā does not itself present these as a numbered ladder. Bands belong to the interpretation layer and are given only where the fit seemed clear.
